facts.text: Timber Cove began as a doghole port in 1856, with a hotel, store, post office, and a lumber chute that first appeared that decade.
The single trough chute on the northwest bluff loaded schooners with cord wood, fence posts, railroad ties, tan bark, and produce in 1876.
Between 1868 and 1874, historians recorded 481 schooner cargos transshipped through Timber Cove’s chute.
In 1921 Ernest Saltzig replaced the original slide chute with a wire chute transplanted from Fort Ross, still located between the Boat Landing and Inn.
The 93‑foot Bufano statue, known as the Expanding Universe, overlooks the Pacific from a bluff within the Timber Cove Resort grounds.
By 1925 lumbering ended and ranching and dairy farming became the main industry, a common shift along the Sonoma coast.
